Government Code 7522, Section F1 requires the governing body of a public agency, or in our case, the City council, to certify the necessity to re employ a retired individual within six months of their retirement in order to perform critically needed services. This action must be facilitated in public hearing, hence the item before you this evening. The San Rafael Police Department's communication center operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year. The Police Department's communication center provides essential public safety communication services, including our 911 answering point. Communication center staff also provide additional support services for the organization. Currently, the communication center is understaffed by two line level positions in addition to a lead dispatcher position, creating three vacancies amongst 10 positions that are funded in the Police Department's budget. Despite our ongoing recruitment efforts, both within the Police Department and the Human Resources Department, communications center staffing remains understaffed, largely due to employee turnover. Compounding the staffing challenges in our communication centers, or, excuse me, our communication center include personal leaves, fmla, protected leaves, excuse me, protected leaves, as well as vacation that all of these create additional burden on this critical but short staffed unit. This item proposes the Council's authorization to certify the necessity to rehire a San Rafael City employee in response to these critical staffing shortages. As indicated in your staff report, this recommendation is grounded in compliance with California government code. While the city's Police Department typically relies on hourly or per diem dispatchers to cover shifts, to provide vacation relief and to support special events, others in this role have had a more substantial break in service which does not require council approval if it's been in excess of a six month break. The staff report identifies the previous employee that the Police Department seeks to rehire as Andorra Lee. Ms. Lee brings over 30, excuse me, three decades of public safety dispatch experience as well as contemporary familiarity with police operations, and this will serve the organization in bridging our existing staffing gap. Moreover, the Department will benefit from decades of institutional knowledge, operational expertise, immediate shift relief, minimizing these staffing challenges and relieving the organization of compounding of the compounding overtime burden. If authorized, Ms. Lee's limited term appointment, which is capped at 960 hours per fiscal year, would provide immediate relief to communication staff without any downtime or training impacts. There's no physical impact fiscal impact resulting from this action. If approved, the associated labor expenses are already budgeted in the Police Department's budget for per diem hours or hourly hours that exist within our budget. While limited options exist in the staff report, the staff recommends that the City Council adopt the resolution to certify and authorize the contingent hire of retired City of San Rafael employee Andorra Lee for a duration not to exceed 960 hours per fiscal year. And with that, I'll be available for any questions you might have.
